# Belinda

## Overview

- **Age:** Fourteen (in Volume 2)  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Origin:** St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010)</sub>
- **Role:** Handmaiden and domestic helper  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c28 P56](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0056)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Belinda the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P61](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0061), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>; Leonora  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042)</sub>

## Appearance

She has freckles on her face, a snub nose, and a broad mouth with exceptionally wide smiles. Earlier in her youth, she constantly wore extremely blue ribbon bows in her hair, though she stopped wearing them as she grew older into a mature young woman.

_Sources: [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007), [v4 c3 P37](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0037)_

## Personality

Belinda is energetic, joyful, obedient, and intensely devoted to her mistress. She possesses a hearty chuckle and an affectionate disposition, though she can express quick indignation when feeling excluded by those she considers close friends. She is highly agreeable and holds a deep, nostalgic attachment to her home island.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P73](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0073), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c28 P18](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0018), [v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048), [v2 c28 P56](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0056), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010)_

## History

At fourteen years old, Belinda lived at Echo Cottage serving Miss Rosalind Penrose in exchange for room, board, and clothing. Though her true name was Leonora Bowman, Miss Rosalind dubbed her 'Belinda the Fourth' to match her older sisters who had previously served there. She maintained a joyful household with Miss Rosalind, routinely indulging in late-night treats despite wall-mounted newspaper warnings. She formed a warm friendship with Nell Harcourt and Isolde, enthusiastically welcoming them during their visits and helping prepare Echo Cottage for Miss Rosalind's wedding. Following Miss Rosalind's marriage to Mr. Stanhope, Belinda moved with them to Boston, where she suffered from intense homesickness and missed St. Brendan's Island. She later returned to Echo Cottage for summer visits as she grew into a young woman. Eventually, she married Tom, a bricklayer, and returned to attend Nell Harcourt's wedding, where she cheerfully threw rice and old shoes as the newlyweds departed.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P61](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0061), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029), [v2 c28 P18](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0018), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007), [v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010), [v3 c40 P0](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0000), [v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042), [v4 c4 P16](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- Real name is Leonora Bowman  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Youngest of Mrs. Bowman's daughters  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Lived at Echo Cottage in exchange for room, board, and garments  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Succeeded her older sisters Belinda, Julietta, and Evelina in service to Miss Rosalind  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Married Tom, an agreeable bricklayer  <sub>[v4 c3 P9](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0009), [v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042)</sub>

## Quotes

> Please, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, it can easily be noticed that a secret exists between you and Miss Rosalind, and I believe, asking for your forgiveness if I am being overly bold, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, that withholding it from me is truly unkind, considering how close we have all been as friends.  <sub>[v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048)</sub>

> I’m truly happy about that. People at home claimed I had one, though I figured they probably merely wished to annoy me. A Yankee accent is something I don't desire. I have nothing at all against the Yankees, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. They are genuinely civilized. However, I would choose old St. Brendan’s Island over them any day.  <sub>[v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010)</sub>

> Gracious, no, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. I would not have any idea who he was referring to if he did. Naturally, at the time we were wed he was required to recite, 'I take thee, Leonora,’ and I swear to you, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, I have carried the most terrible impression ever since that he was not speaking to me and I have not been properly wedded whatsoever. And thus you are about to be wedded your own self, Miss Harcourt, ma’am? I ever imagined I should enjoy being wed to a physician. It would be exceedingly useful whenever the little ones contracted measles and croup. Tom is merely a bricklayer, yet he possesses a truly fine disposition. When I remarked to him, says I, 'Tom, may I attend Miss Harcourt’s wedding? I intend to go regardless, yet I should prefer to possess your permission,’ he simply responds, 'Suit yourself, Belinda, and you’ll suit me.’ That is a truly agreeable sort of spouse to possess, Miss Harcourt, ma’am.  <sub>[v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042)</sub>
